generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the sport subjects you are already studying. Every module across the School of Sport sets assessments, marks them against criteria, and gives you feedback; the students who understand that cycle, and run it on purpose, are the ones whose lab reports, session plans and case studies improve from one assignment to the next rather than repeating the same mistakes. In the School of Sport you often have more say than you might expect, since courses commonly invite you to help shape assessment, so understanding how it works lets you use that voice well. Treat what follows as being about your own reports, plans and practical work, not about study in the abstract.

The same brief, standard, feedback and next-task cycle runs through professional sport too. Whether you go into coaching, performance science, sport management or rehabilitation, your work is judged against a standard, you receive feedback, and you carry it into what you do next. Learning from that feedback and iterating your practice on the back of it is a habit you keep long after you graduate.
